rationale: Repair of the concrete failure in inputs/previous-feedback.txt (trial-93aa5d5fc1-param-4fabdd0b, same boundary group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb, same plan). That attempt passed quality and the step constraint (139.51/143.73 vs limit 144.80 ms) but was rejected for paired_gain_not_above_noise (0.41 vs 6.67 ms bound) because the CUDA-graph replay path never executed: after the first parent-reference invocation, every invocation ran fallback:parent:capture_failed:RuntimeError on both ranks, so the measured 'gain' was parent-vs-parent noise. candidate_diagnostics-4123e6d6 records the exact exception at the previous candidate.py:262 segment_loss.backward() inside torch.cuda.graph capture: 'During CUDA graph capture, autograd node torch::autograd::AccumulateGrad has a stale reference to the default stream (stream 0) from warmup. This will invalidate the capture because cudaStreamWaitEvent on the default stream pulls a non-capturing stream into the graph. To fix, either: (a) Run warmup on the same stream that capture will use, or (b) Delete references to the loss / autograd graph (e.g. del loss) before capture, or (c) Call torch.autograd.graph.set_override_stale_capture_stream(True)'. This attempt applies exactly those documented fixes, verified available in the measured worker (torch 2.13.0+cu129, /root/autodl-tmp/dev-venv/bin/python): (a) one explicit side stream S now carries both the eager warmup (with torch.cuda.stream(S)) and every capture via torch.cuda.graph(graph, pool=pool, stream=S) - the shared-pool/same-stream pattern torch 2.13's graph docstring itself requires - instead of warming on an unrelated stream while torch.cuda.graph captured on its own internal stream; (b) warmup loss/output/autograd references are deleted before capture and captured static losses are stored detached; (c) torch.autograd.graph.set_override_stale_capture_stream(True) is enabled around the capture section to redirect the remaining stale default-stream AccumulateGrad references (created by invocation-1's parent backward on stream 0) to the capturing stream, restored to the documented process-initial False in a finally block. Everything else keeps the previously validated design: precomputed 4D causal mask passthrough (transformers 5.16.1 _preprocess_mask_arguments returns an already-prepared 4D mask as-is; eager attention only adds it, attn_weights + attention_mask; bypasses the masking_utils.py:603 unpinned CPU-scalar copy that killed the earlier trial-f684195486), live bit-exact mask verification on current inputs before any capture attempt, per-parameter primed in-place gradient buffers, one graph per no_sync micro-batch in a shared pool replayed in capture order, static input buffers refreshed from the current inputs every invocation, eager final micro-batch through the unmodified DDP reducer (all 13 fp32 bucket allreduces, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, broadcast_buffers=False untouched), SGD (lr=0.001, foreach=False) step and the single final torch.cuda.synchronize, optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) inside the timed boundary exactly as the parent. Semantics I verified myself on the installed stack on CPU (no ad hoc GPU use): two-rank gloo DDP with the exact adapter flags shows the interleaving pattern (prime standalone per-parameter grad buffers -> three raw-module backwards -> one synced DDP backward -> SGD step, after a prior full-parent invocation and weight reset, for two consecutive rounds) reproduces loss, micro losses, every gradient and every parameter bit-exactly; the 4D mask tensor is torch.equal to create_causal_mask's output and the masked forward is bit-identical in logits, loss and all gradients; torch.cuda.graph accepts stream= and set_override_stale_capture_stream exists. Why the objective can move (hypothesis to be measured, not assumed): execution_timeline-1221e205 shows rank 0 submitting all 13 matched collectives 10.3-10.7 ms before rank 1, rank 0's first burst kernel running 14.058 ms vs 3.644 ms on rank 1, while the warmed synthetic calibration floors are ~3.536 ms per 28 MB bucket and ~19.383 ms for the 157.5 MB bucket (61.82/62.90 ms rank floors); kernel durations include device waiting, so replay's near-constant early CPU dispatch of the three unsynchronized no_sync micro-batches on both ranks attacks the accumulated submit spread the earlier rank absorbs into its first kernel, moving the max-rank sum from the parent's observed 63.2-77.3 ms endpoints toward the calibrated floors - an expected paired gain of roughly 1-10 ms that may not clear the 6.67/5.65 ms MAD noise bounds; acceptance is measured, not presumed. Residual hazards degrade permanently and safely to the parent reference with distinct route labels (setup_failed:mask_not_bit_exact / setup_failed:warmup_failed:* / capture_failed:* / replay_failed:* / workload_shape_changed / model_replaced / unsupported_signature), the collective-bearing final micro-batch and optimizer step are never re-run by a fallback, both ranks always execute the same eager 13-allreduce final micro-batch so collective participation stays rank-symmetric even under mixed rank success/failure, and this run then acts only as a measured control. Frozen task semantics are unchanged: same batch, sequence length, accumulation steps, effective batch 8, sampling/data, DDP and optimizer configuration, FP32/TF32-off precision, quality thresholds, boundaries and measurement protocol; no precomputed fixture outputs (graphs replay the kernels on the refreshed current inputs every invocation).

setup_work.when: lazy, inside the second project.invoke invocation (documented untimed warmup under the measurement protocol: correctness pass -> warmup 2 -> 5 clean timed repeats -> 3 profiled diagnostics -> inventory pass; the first invocation always runs the pure parent reference, which also rebuilds DDP buckets)
steps: Invocation 1: run the unmodified parent reference and snapshot model/raw_model/parameter identity.
Build 3 causal 4D float32 masks (1,1,128,128) outside capture from arange/where/finfo constants.

Verify mask passthrough bit-exactness live per segment: two no_grad forwards (attention_mask=None vs precomputed 4D mask) compared with torch.equal on loss and logits; any mismatch aborts before any capture (setup_failed:mask_not_bit_exact).

Allocate persistent per-parameter gradient buffers: 124,439,808 fp32 elements = 497,759,232 B (~497.8 MB), kept for the process lifetime; prime parameter.grad onto them and zero via torch._foreach_zero_.

Eager warmup of each no_sync segment (forward + scaled backward) on the single explicit capture stream S (fix a), dropping loss/output references afterwards (fix b); this runs lazy library init and stream-liveness warmup outside capture.

Enable torch.autograd.graph.set_override_stale_capture_stream(True) (fix c), capture one CUDAGraph per no_sync segment (forward + backward) into one shared pool with torch.cuda.graph(graph, pool=pool, stream=S), restore the override to False in a finally block, and assert in-place gradient accumulation (parameter.grad is buffer).

Finish the capture invocation by replaying the graphs on the current inputs and running the eager final micro-batch, SGD step and the single final torch.cuda.synchronize; later invocations are replay-only (refresh static inputs from the current inputs, zero buffers, replay in capture order).
memory: Setup allocation (capture invocation, outside clean timed repeats): ~497.8 MB persistent gradient buffers + ~0.2 MB static masks + ~1.5 KB static int64 inputs + forward/backward intermediates of the warmup.

Retained after setup: one shared CUDA graph private pool holding three whole-network (forward+backward) captures of GPT-2 124M FP32 at micro_batch=1/seq=128; retained graph pool memory increases framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and framework.lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes, and per-run allocation that moved into capture can lower warm-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes without being a physical-memory saving.
No CUDA Graph capture happens inside the clean timed repeats; each repeat refreshes static input buffers from the current inputs and replays, so the workload executes on each invocation.

quality_risks: The replay path has never executed on GPU: both prior trials of this plan failed capture before replay, so their passing quality checks only exercised parent fallback. The interleaving semantics were re-verified bit-exact on two-rank gloo CPU DDP with the exact adapter flags (loss, micro losses, gradients, parameters, across consecutive reset invocations), but GPU-only capture/replay behaviors (stream capture validity, in-place AccumulateGrad accumulation inside the graph, shared-pool replay ordering) are validated only by the framework's bound worker run; any failure falls back permanently to the parent with distinct labels, in which case this attempt is a measured control.

set_override_stale_capture_stream(True) redirects stale stream references during capture; it is restored to the documented process-initial False in a finally block even when capture raises, and it is only enabled around the capture section.

If a timed bucket ever included the capture invocation (the documented protocol places capture in untimed warmup), that one repeat would carry the capture cost; the median-of-5 protocol and the <=1.05x step_ms constraint absorb it, and the previous trial's failed-capture endpoint already measured 139.51/143.73 ms vs the 144.80 ms limit.

Mask equivalence is re-verified on the live current inputs before every capture attempt; if transformers' internal mask ever diverges from the precomputed replica (torch.equal check on loss and logits), the graph path aborts before capture and all invocations use the parent.

The captured static losses are read after replay on the same (default) stream, and buffers are zeroed before replay on that stream, so replay ordering is stream-ordered; a replay failure falls back to the parent for the whole invocation from a clean zero_grad restart, never re-running the collective-bearing final micro-batch.

Both ranks run identical candidate logic, so the exact (atol=0, rtol=0) cross-rank gradient replica check compares two identical replay executions; the vs-serial-reference checks use the frozen tolerances as before.
